title: Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon with stronger cyber and long-horizon agent performance
dek: Carbon leads an independently run composite model index and posts high vendor-reported cyber benchmark scores, but broad access is not yet available.
evidence: Independent Artificial Analysis composite score; Google-reported cybersecurity and alignment evaluations
takeaway: Separate the independently measured general-capability gain from vendor cyber and safety claims; run permission-bound, end-to-end security tasks before trusting autonomous fixes.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Finding a vulnerability, proving exploitability and producing a safe patch are different tasks. A model can score well on one without closing the full remediation loop.

paragraphs: Different cyber tasks: Finding a vulnerability, proving exploitability and producing a safe patch are different tasks. A model can score well on one without closing the full remediation loop.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon as the successor to Gemini 4 Argon, targeting coding, cybersecurity and agent workflows that can persist through multi-step engineering work.

Initial access starts with selected cyber defenders and trusted partners. General developer API and consumer access were not available at announcement; Google is conducting pre-release safety testing.

Google lists $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input priced 95% below regular input. After the introductory period, stated prices rise to $4 and $20 per million respectively.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Artificial Analysis independently evaluates its nine-benchmark Intelligence Index v5.0. Gemini 4 Carbon at High effort scores 59 versus Claude Opus 5.5 at Max with 58. The one-point lead is not a universal win across workloads.

Google reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (vulnerability discovery), 54.8% on ExploitGym (exploitation), and 71.0% on CWE-bench (patching). Google says these cyber benchmark runs were evaluated without guardrails; they do not measure a guarded production deployment.

Google reports 0.0% successful cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 0.4% cheating attempts, 0.0% attack success on Gray Swan's indirect prompt-injection evaluation, and roughly half as many unsupported claims as Argon in internal tests. Zero observed successes is not proof of zero risk outside those test sets.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Score discovery, exploit confirmation, patch correctness, regression tests and authorized deployment separately. A high exploit score can increase risk unless tool permissions and review gates are explicit.
The index spans coding, science, general knowledge and knowledge work. Reproduce representative tasks with fixed effort, tools, time limits and cost accounting before changing model routing.

paragraphs: Evaluate the full repair chain: Score discovery, exploit confirmation, patch correctness, regression tests and authorized deployment separately. A high exploit score can increase risk unless tool permissions and review gates are explicit.
